sections.content:
42,510 people

were counted on the census as "registered specialist nurses" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Registered specialist nurses provide specialised nursing care and plan ongoing treatment for the sick, injured and others in need of care, take responsibility for patients within their sphere of practice, assist medical doctors with their tasks, and work with other healthcare professionals.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "registered specialist nurses" there were more women than men (88.3% compared with 11.7%).

This means "registered specialist nurses" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 11.7% and women made up 88.3% of "registered specialist nurses"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "registered specialist nurses" included:

  • educational support assistants
  • playworkers
  • other registered nursing professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "registered specialist nurses", 16.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "registered specialist nurses" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "registered specialist nurses" included:

  • education managers
  • train and tram drivers
  • health care practice managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "registered specialist nurses" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "registered specialist nurses" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "registered specialist nurses", 10.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.6% compared with 28.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.2%) than self-employed (1.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
